A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Learning to Be Cautious. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–C are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, experiments, and displays can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-based contextual-bandit and driving-gridworld experiments, including action frequencies, classification accuracy, collision statistics, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds help-reward sensitivity results in Appendix B.1.3.

M1.justification: The neural-network reward ensemble, k-of-N reward selection, regret matching, architectures, and training losses are retained. The new main-text Algorithm 1 summarizes the procedure already documented in v2; the corresponding appendix pseudocode remains as Algorithm 2.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST digits, Fashion-MNIST, EMNIST letters, and the driving gridworld, retaining the same tasks and all-images/single-image regimes. The added reward sweeps vary parameters within existing tasks rather than introduce new data or input environments.

E2.justification: Retained comparisons use the same Optim(ˆr) baseline and k-of-N configurations. The 1-of-20 configuration added to Figure 3's legend was already evaluated in v2's appendix. Additional discussion of alternative RL approaches does not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1.3 adds experiments using help rewards of 0.1 and 0.5 around the original 0.25, and 0.02 and 0.2 around the original conditional-help reward of 0.05. The retained experiments preserve their data splits, architectures, training budgets, metrics, and CFR iteration counts.

E4.justification: v3 adds a targeted sensitivity study testing how the help reward affects help-seeking, action selection, and classification accuracy in two existing tasks. The convergence plots, training-data-size analysis, and confusion matrices were already present in v2.

E5.justification: Figure 2 replaces the baseline's 95% confidence-interval display with violin plots described as showing variation; similar displays accompany the new sensitivity results. Both versions specify ten MNIST repetitions and five driving-gridworld repetitions, so an increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: New reward-sensitivity results include 1-of-20 single-image accuracy/help frequencies of 98.83%/0.00% at reward 0.1 and 92.37%/7.63% at reward 0.5 (v3 Tables 2 and 4). These are additional settings, not same-setting performance changes. Original tables and appendix graphics retain their results, although new B.1.2 reverses the stated digit-like-letter help-seeking trend despite the unchanged heatmap.

T1.justification: The MDP definitions, reward-uncertainty and transition-certainty assumptions, Lemma 1, Theorems 1–3, and Appendix C proofs retain the same mathematical content and bounds. Their typesetting and placement change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: progressively demanding caution tasks, learned caution through reward ensembles and robust optimization, and the extension of k-of-N CFR to continuing MDPs. The sensitivity evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations linking help-reward sensitivity to utility, a claim about ensemble cost being independent of state-space size, and an excessive-conservatism caveat. New B.1.2 attributes digit-like-letter behavior to heightened epistemic uncertainty and monitoring, conflicting with the retained heatmap. B.1.3 also interprets increasing help rewards as improving accuracy despite contrary table entries.

D1.justification: v3 introduces an explicit GitHub code link in the abstract and Section 4. Appendix B removes v2's descriptions of the pretrained-model directory and Google Drive location for models/data. These are changes to access information; the PDFs do not establish actual resource availability. Existing implementation and hardware details remain.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds discussion and citations for Liu et al. (2022), Yu et al. (2022), Ying et al. (2022), and Yang et al. (2021), contrasting their constraints or risk formulations with the paper's setting. Section 4 also adds an explicit rationale for excluding alternative baseline families. The central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained with local editing. v3 merges conclusions and future work, introduces numbered experimental subsections in Appendix B, adds a compact algorithm summary, and updates author affiliations and publication text.

P2.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the displays: Figure 2 becomes larger stacked violin panels, Figure 3's legend is corrected, and Figures 5–6 add sensitivity panels. Experimental figures and tables are grouped before Appendix C instead of interrupting its proofs. The algorithm gains a main-text display, while Tables 3 and 5 duplicate the original default-reward results.

improvement.justification: The sensitivity experiments, more readable figure organization, and explicit code link provide useful gains. However, new Appendix B.1.2 reverses the behavior shown in the retained heatmap, and B.1.3 claims improving accuracy despite Tables 2–4 showing substantial decreases for cautious settings. The revision therefore adds useful evidence while introducing substantive misinterpretations, leaving its net effect on overall quality unclear.
